newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NBP has no comment on zloty, interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Polish NBP has no comment on zloty, interest rates.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland has no comment on the zloty's recent fall against the currency basket or on interest rate levels, the deputy central bank president Witold Kozinski said on Tuesday.
"At this moment please do not ask me about the exchange rate or about increasing interest rates because right now I have no comment in this matter," Kozinski told a news conference.

The zloty has hit all time lows against the currency basket on Tuesday, weakening more than two percentage points since opening and about four percent over the last week, amid speculative zloty sales and foreign investor withdrawal.
Dealers have been looking for the central bank to stage a currency-selling intervention or to indicate a level at which it wanted the zloty to trade to give the local unit support.
Late last week the central bank president Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said a further tightening of monetary policy was needed to cool rampant domestic demand.
Earlier in July the central bank increased market rates by nearly half a point in order to stop booming credit expansion.
